candidates.rationale: Positions today's dollar volume within its own 63-day high-low band (a liquidity stochastic): sitting near the floor means trading interest is drying up, implying a thinner book and wider effective spreads that should command a return premium, while sitting near the ceiling reflects a transient attention spike that tends to fade.

Correlates signed daily returns with the stock's own trailing volume percentile over a quarter; persistent positive co-movement means price gains are being confirmed by broadening participation (a durable, well-supported trend), while decoupling flags moves happening on unconfirmed, light volume that are prone to reverse.

A directional-efficiency ratio: net 15-day price change divided by the cumulative intraday range traveled to get there. High efficiency means information is being absorbed with little wasted back-and-forth (deep, liquid price discovery); low efficiency means the same trading activity is pure chop from contested price discovery, a state that tends to resolve directionally once the disagreement clears.

High-margin firms have durable pricing power, so when such a name shows an unusual own-history spike in short-run range volatility it more plausibly reflects real information being priced in than noise trading; margin quality acts as a filter on how much conviction to assign to a volatility jump.

Tests whether a stock's relative liquidity ranking and its relative volatility-range ranking move together over half a year; sustained alignment marks a durable shift into an actively-traded, higher-attention regime that should persist, while decoupling (volatility rising without matching liquidity support) flags a fragile, unsupported move.

Crosses capital-efficiency quality with an acute, 5-day spike in a stock's own range percentile: a sharp volatility burst in a fundamentally efficient firm more likely reflects real news being digested by informed capital, whereas the identical burst in a low-quality firm is more likely noise trading with no follow-through.

A range-volatility term structure: when very recent (5-day) range volatility is compressed relative to the 63-day baseline, the stock sits in a temporary liquidity-calm regime that historically precedes mean-reversion in required risk premia, while the reverse (recent range volatility spiking above baseline) signals an acute liquidity-stress episode.

Conditions a 5-day price-reversal signal on the stock's cross-sectional liquidity rank, since the balance between mechanical bid-ask-bounce reversal and genuine information-driven continuation differs systematically between deeply-traded, efficiently-priced names and thin ones.

Under the mixture-of-distributions view, a large realized price move paired with a fast climb in the stock's own 42-day volume percentile is the joint signature of a genuine information event, distinguishing conviction moves where both legs fire from volume drifting up with no price reaction or a price move on stagnant relative participation.

Counts how many of the last 21 days had volume above the stock's own 63-day baseline: requiring sustained, not one-off, elevated participation filters out single-day spike noise to isolate a genuine, durable upgrade in the stock's trading-interest and liquidity regime.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Changing only the outer time-series statistic (e.g. TS_STD vs TS_MEAN) on an otherwise-identical guarded ratio still collides on archive_subtree (7 shared nodes this round) — the inner expression needs to change too, not just the outer wrapper.
  2. The 'difference of two CS_RANK((high-low)/(X+eps))' family with a 5-day normalizer window is archive-saturated — two independent proposals this round shared 5 and 10 nodes with existing accepts. Retire this exact shape or move to a materially longer window.
  3. Of all $return-based cheap_screen rejects this round, a 40-day return sum normalized by 21-day range came closest to clearing (|t| 0.82) — a decayed or reweighted version of that specific pairing is worth one more try before dropping return-sum-over-range ideas entirely.
  4. Several within-round duplicates reused the same 5-day dollar_volume/range ratio and the same-length roa/roe delta shape — vary window length or operator before resubmitting a shape already tried earlier in the same run.
  5. Four of sixteen rejects this round came from one mechanical pattern: swapping only the numerator field (return, close-open, high-open, high-close) inside TS_MEAN(numerator / ($dollar_volume + eps), ~10 days) while holding the denominator and window fixed. This keeps rho at 0.86-0.97 against each other or a plain dollar-volume mean, and the same guarded-denominator subtree also trips archive_subtree elsewhere. Treat this ratio family as exhausted; a new candidate needs a different denominator construction, not a different numerator.
  6. Inside CS_RANK(fundamental) * TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 63), both $earnings_per_share (rho 0.804) and price-scaled $roe (rho 0.895) collapsed back onto the archived $roe version. EPS now behaves like a member of the ROA/ROE profitability cluster for correlation purposes, and dividing by $close does not escape it. $asset_turnover on the same leg stayed independent and accepted (2.016); vary the accounting dimension, not the profitability field or its price-scaling.
  7. A dollar-volume-normalized intraday-move ratio and a stochastic-style range-position ratio shared no operators, fields, or windows yet hit rho 0.859. Passing archive_subtree is not evidence a candidate will clear correlation; weigh what real-world signal a new shape approximates against archive members that answer something similar, not just ones that look similar on paper.
  8. Bare CS_RANK/RANK of $earnings_per_share and $book_per_share (no TS_* window, no delta) cleared coverage cleanly, including the round's best fitness (6.794) and two more accepts. Coverage risk for these fields is specific to windowing or differencing them, not to using the level; don't discount an EPS- or book-per-share-anchored proposal on coverage grounds unless it is also windowed.
  9. TS_RANK($high - $low, 63) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($volume, 21)) accepted at 4.998 with no fundamental leg at all, the round's second-best. The winning assignment put TS_RANK on the leg that varies within a name over time and CS_RANK on a cross-sectional dispersion stat of the other leg; don't default to requiring a fundamental partner in every price/volume product.
  10. TS_CORR(ABS($return), TS_RANK($volume, 21), 21) accepted at 4.507. Rank-transforming the volume leg is what rescues a return/volume correlation; raw-return-vs-raw-volume stays a dead end, but the fix is TS_RANK on volume, not abandoning the pairing.
  11. The fundamental-minus-raw-leg rank spread set a new round-best (6.794, EPS minus a bounded price-position ratio); keep exploring bounded price ratios as the 'other' leg, not just volume/range ranks. The one spread that failed did so on coverage from a 252-day window on the non-fundamental leg, not the fundamental choice; cap any window in a spread at 63 days regardless of which leg carries it.
  12. Two crossover children were rejected for donating only 2 shared nodes from a normal 5-node parent instead of exactly 3, both against the same RANK($roa) * RANK($dollar_volume) parent, both replacing one whole branch and keeping only the other operator-plus-leaf pair. Target an exactly-3-node shared subtree with each parent, not a whole branch or a single leaf.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
Leave `parent_ids` empty and `changed_node` empty for EXPLORE.
